title: A 1951-2005 degree-day relation kept forecast skill for US county corn and soybean yields in 2006-2025 but not for cotton; training signal fraction, not response class, ranked 70 state-crop skills
abstract: Question: do the training signal fraction and a level update, rather than the response class, predict which climate-response relations keep forecast skill? Approach: we froze and timestamped a plan before we loaded yields. We refitted the Schlenker-Roberts (2009) degree-day model (county effects, state quadratic trends, degree days 10 C to T* and above T*, precipitation) on 1951-2005 NASS county yields with nClimGrid-daily weather. Then we scored 2006-2025 forecasts against a frozen trend (R1) and a trailing 10-year trend (R2). Results: the frozen relation gave clear gains for corn (skill 0.19, 95% year-block interval 0.13 to 0.28) and soybeans (0.18, 0.11 to 0.23), against the class rule. A frozen slope with an updated level (M2) gave 0.32 for both against R2. Upland cotton had a training signal fraction of 0.13 but no clear gain (-0.04; M2 0.04, -0.14 to 0.15), against the signal rule. Across 70 state-crop units, forward skill increased with the training signal fraction (Spearman 0.55, permutation p = 0.0001); the median ratio of skill to signal fraction was 1.00. Frozen trends missed later yield levels by up to 0.3 log units, and weather explained almost none of this drift. The heat slope weakened after 2005 for corn (-0.65% to -0.47% per degree day) and cotton (-0.74% to -0.23%), so a growing heat sensitivity was not supported. An exploratory pseudo-forward test inside 1951-2005 matched the later crop-level skills within 0.03, including the cotton failure. Limitations: realized season weather, county-average temperatures, fewer NASS counties after 2008, three crops only, and exploratory section 6.

citations.reason: We test its response-class rule (not supported for corn and soybeans) and its signal-fraction and level-update proposals (supported for unit ranking and level update; a fixed signal threshold failed for cotton). We reuse its six-test summary table.
